preconditions.description: The number of elements n in set S is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(S) == n and all(1 <= s <= 200000 for s in S) and len(set(S)) == n
preconditions.description: The set S contains exactly n distinct integers, each between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output integer x is the largest non-negative integer such that a valid magical permutation exists for the range [0, 2^x - 1].
The output permutation contains exactly 2^x integers.
The output permutation contains every integer from 0 to 2^x - 1 exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all((permutation[i] ^ permutation[i+1]) in S for i in range(len(permutation) - 1))
postconditions.description: For every pair of consecutive elements in the permutation, their bitwise XOR is an element present in the set S.

postconditions.expression: not any((permutation[i] ^ permutation[i+1]) in S for i in range(len(permutation) - 1)) if x == 0 else True
postconditions.description: If x is 0, the permutation has length 1 (only 0), so the condition on consecutive pairs is vacuously true; otherwise, the condition in Q4 must hold.
